newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber unchanged in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber unchanged in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade March SIR20 offer prices were unchanged in slow trading on Thursday despite small buying from Europe and the U.S., traders said.
March SIR20 was unchanged at 54.625 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan and Surabaya from the morning level, but was slightly higher than Wednesday prices of 54.50 U.S. cents/lb.
In Palembang, offers were quoted at 54.50 U.S. cents/lb, while in Pontianak and Jambi prices were higher at 54.25 U.S. cents/lb against 53.875 U.S. cents/lb on Wednesday.
"There are some buying interest in the market, but overall activity is still quiet because of the extended Eid al-Fitr celebration," said one trader.
Traders earlier said there had been some sporadic buying from European and U.S. buyers, but orders only reached between 100 and 200 tonnes.
"Some producers are not so enthusiastic in selling the goods because they expect prices to go up further," said one dealer.
"We are glad to see how prices recover now after softening before the Eid al-Fitr. There were traders who sold rubber at 52.50 U.S. cents/lb then," he added.
Traders said supply remained tight because farmers had not returned to work after the celebration. Indonesians usually return to work a week after the festivity ends.
